best_plan.name: p2
best_plan.rationale: p2 had the best accuracy by a wide margin and was stable across two runs, with relative error about 0.064 versus 0.286 for p1 and 0.786 for p3. Although p2 costs more than p1, the quality improvement is substantial, while p3 shows that similarly priced cheaper models can be much worse. So p2 gives the best observed cost-quality trade-off for estimating the positive-review fraction for taken_3.

plan_codes.p1:
pipeline = PhysicalPipeline(plan_name, "Reviews.csv", load_data("Reviews.csv"))
pipeline.filter(lambda row: row["idx"] == "taken_3")
pipeline.sem_map(
    [{
        "name": "positive_score",
        "type": float,
        "description": "Return 1.0 if the review text is overall positive toward the movie, else 0.0."
    }],
    model=pz.Model.GOOGLE_GEMINI_2_5_FLASH_LITE,
    depends_on=["reviewText"]
)
pipeline.groupby([], ["average"], ["positive_score"])
pipeline.project(["average(positive_score)"])
pipeline
